title: How Countries Can Strengthen Their Energy Security
figure_ref: Exhibit 2 related reported narrative (editorial approximate-share bar; original chart not inspected)
business_context: BCG frames energy import dependence as a strategic vulnerability amid geopolitical and market disruptions. The public article states that about 60% of OECD countries import more than half of their energy. The publication does not provide exact country-level data or a precise measurement year in the passage used.
key_message: Approximately 60% of OECD countries depend on imports for more than half their energy.
so_what: Energy-security strategy should identify exposure to imports at the national level before choosing diversification, domestic capacity, or resilience policies.
encoding: x=0–100% of OECD country count; stacked segments=import dependence; approximate direct labels

values.label: Import >50% of energy
values.denominator: OECD countries; n and survey year undisclosed

data_recipe: Set the OECD country membership and measurement year before collecting country-level energy balances.
Compute net-import dependence consistently: imports, exports, production and total energy supply definitions must align.
Count countries above the 50% threshold, with the denominator explicitly known.
Label rounded aggregate shares as approximate; compute a residual only as an approximate complement.
Use a 100% stacked bar for an editorial summary; do not present it as the source's original exhibit.
message_conditions: 60% is a rounded estimate, not exact observed country count.
40% is derived as an approximate complement and not separately reported.
Missing country denominator, date and import-definition details prevent precision or confidence bounds.
No inference about energy volume shares, import values or individual country risk from this aggregate count.
design_moves: Kind stacked_share; color/layout/context configurable via THEME and CONTEXT
Direct labels and careful unit/denominator distinction
All positions computed from data and series order
